newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PRESIDENT'S RULE TO BE EXTENDED IN UTTAR PRADESH

The United Front (UF) steering committee decided to continue President's rule in Uttar Pradesh (U.P.) till the formation of a secular government in the State. The UF move has dashed the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) hopes of being invited to prove its majority in the U.P. assembly. Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav and BKKP party chief Ajit Singh were instrumental to the decision. Both leaders said inviting the BJP to form a government at this stage would make other parties vulnerable to splits. This was accepted by the UF leadership which agreed to extend President's Rule in U.P.
The Times Of India
FORMER MINISTER SHEILA KAUL FINED SIX MLN RUPEES

In a bid to make ministers more accountable, the Supreme Court slapped an exemplary fine on the former urban development minister Sheila Kaul for her alleged role in the multi-million housing scam. The court has asked Kaul to deposit six million rupees with the finance ministry for having allotted a number of kiosks and shops in Delhi in excess of her discretionary powers. The court had earlier held that the allotments made by her were arbitrary, unconstitutional and liable to be quashed.
The Hindustan Times
ANDHRA PRADESH CYCLONE TOLL CROSSES 1,000

The death toll in the cyclone that hit the coastal belt of Andhra Pradesh has reached 1,000. The cyclone is said to have destroyed the property worth 20 billion rupees. There has also been fears of the spread of an epidemic in the waterlogged areas of the state. State chief minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has urged the federal government to treat the cyclone as a national calamity and offer commensurate assistance. Sources say the federal government's assistance of 500 million rupees, and another 20 million rupees from the prime minister's relief fund, has already been released.
The Economic Times
NATIONAL SECURITIES DEPOSITORY INAUGURATED

U.S. Ambassador Frank Wisner described the setting up of the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) as a significant step forward in the development of India's capital markets. Wisner, who joined Finance Minister P. Chidambaram for the inauguration of NSDL, said the depository would provide the foreign institutional investors with a sense of security. The U.S. has contributed to the creation of NSDL through funding provided to Price Waterhouse by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) under its FIRE project. The FIRE project provides U.S. expertise in the form of technical assistance for bringing India's securities markets closer to international standards. USAID will contribute up to $20 million over the life of the project.
OIL IMPORT BILL ESTIMATE HIKED TO $ 9.6 BLN

The oil ministry has hiked its estimates of the oil import bill for the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) to a new high of $9.6 billion, compared with the initial estimate of $7.59 billion. The bill last year was $7.10 billion. Official sources said this was largely on account of a steep fall in domestic crude production. Crude imports are expected to be nearly 33.2 million tonnes and petro-products nearly 22.1 million tonnes. This compares with 27.2 million tonne crude and 20.3 million tonne products last year.
REPOS NET THREE BLN RUPEES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a cut-off rate of 5.48 percent on 14-day repos auctioned on Friday, absorbing three billion in the process. The inflow of 3.1 billion rupees into the system on November 9, 1996 is likely to flood the money markets with excess liquidity, dealers said. The trend was reflected in the rising prices on government securities after the repo-rate announcement. According to sources, the RBI was using the repo rate as an interest rate indicator for the short end of the markets. Dealers said the RBI had set a lower cut-off rate at 5.58 percent to signal lower interest rates. Absorbing excess liquidity was a secondary concern, they felt.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS ASKED TO REDUCE COST OF BORROWING

Finance minister P. Chidambaram asked financial institutions (FIs) to cut down their cost of borrowings. FI sources said the finance minister gave them clear indication to lower the lending rates for which the financial intermediaries would have to reduce their cost of resources. The FIs recently announced a cut in their prime lending rate from 17 to 16.5 percent along with a reduction in the interest band from 4.0 to 3.5 percent. This would force the FIs to offer lower coupons on the instruments they mobilised resources through, sources added.
TWENTY STEEL PLANT PROPOSALS CLEARED

Steel and Mines Minister B. P. Baishya informed that financial institutions had cleared the proposals for 20 new steel plants involving an expenditure of 200 billion rupees. This would add an additional capacity of 11.20 million tonnes of steel by year 2000, he said. Proposals for setting up eight more steel plants with a further capacity of four million tonnes with an expenditure of 90 billion rupees are also on cards. The new steel units and the modernisation of the units of the Steel Authority of India would help the country produce up to 37 million tonnes of steel by 2000 AD, said the minister.
BANKING SECTOR LOOPHOLES TO BE PROBED

The Parliamentary standing committee on finance will probe the loopholes in the banking system that led to bank-frauds and violations of the Reserve Bank of India guidelines during the last one year. The committee is also expected to look into the large volume of bank credit given under political influence. It will begin a series of talks with all bank managements starting next week for the purpose. The Parliamentary standing committee on finance normally deals with the government's budgetary aspects.
MANUFACTURING FIRMS GO SLOW ON FUND RAISING

Fresh industrial activity, as reflected in the number of manufacturing projects going public for fund raising, declined during the first half of 1996/97 (April-March). During the same period, the non-manufacturing and finance companies accounted for 50 percent of the total funds raised in the capital markets. For the first half of 1996/97, projects worth only 44.1 billion rupees entered the markets to raise funds, as against total raisings of 140.4 billion rupees in 1995/96. In 1994/95, projects worth 381.8 billion rupees had gone to the public. According to statistics, fiscal 1996/97 may end up with projects worth 88 billion rupees, only half that of last year's figure and about one-fifth of the 1994/95 mark.
Financial Express
EXPORT IMPORT BANK CAPITAL HIKE APPROVED

The cabinet has approved proposals to increase the Exim Bank's authorised capital to 20 billion rupees from the present five billion rupees and restructure Andrew Yule & Co. According to official sources, the Exim Bank Act 1981 would be amended to give effect to the increase in the bank's authorised capital. The increase is to provide the bank with adequate capital base to help it fund its future business growth and raise external resources at competitive rates. The Andrew Yule restructuring would involve spinning off of the company's belting and engineering divisions and converting them into separate joint venture companies. The government holds a 63 percent stake in the company.
INDUSTRY MINISTRY RULES OUT DECLINE IN INTEREST RATES

The industry ministry held the government's heavy borrowing from the market responsible for the current credit squeeze for the corporate and ruled out any decline in interest rate in the medium term. The government was withdrawing more than the total credit created by the commercial banks system. With the government's entry into the money market, the interest rate on gilt securities acted as the bench mark for prime lending rates (PLR). Given that the bench mark lending rate was shaped by the gilt security rate, there was no chance of PLR coming down in the medium term, the ministry said. Heavy borrowing by the government from the banks acted against any funds being available to the corporate sector, it added.
CHEMPLAST IN TALKS WITH MARUBENI

Sanmar group owned Chemplast is in talks with Marubeni India, the wholly-owned subsidiary of the Japanese multinational, for its $50 million textile project near Madras. Marubeni India is likely to sign a pact next week. A consortium comprising Gtosi of Italy and U.S. based Swift Spinning will help Marubeni supply equipment for the project. The finalisation of the agreement will help Marubeni India supply high precision plant equipment to Chemplast.
EXPORTS TO EAST EUROPEAN NATIONS DECLINING

India is slowly being edged out of the markets in Russia, the CIS countries and some in the European Union. According to the latest country-wise analysis of exports by the commerce ministry, India's exports to the East European countries showed a negative growth of 22.2 percent in April-July 1996 over the last corresponding period. India's exports to the Russian federation and other east European countries declined from $334.9 million to $296.7 million (1.4 percent) in the case of the former and from $158.09 million to $74.02 million (53.2 percent) in the case of the latter in the above period. India's exports to EU rose by only 1.3 percent from $2,653.97 million to $2688.63 million.
The Economic Times
PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE TAKES CHARGE OF INFRASTRUCTURE

The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) has decided to directly monitor quarterly performance of the infrastructure sector. Sources said PMO would directly interact with the National Informatics Centre to monitor electricity generation, crude production, coal, railways, steel, cement, ports, telecommunications and fertilisers. The decision was taken in view of the economic slowdown reflected in the poor performance of infrastructure in the first quarter of the current financial year, PMO sources said.
Business Standard
RELIANCE PLANS TO FLOAT 100-YEAR YANKEE BOND

The Reliance Industries Ltd has sought the finance ministry's nod to raise $340 million U.S. bond for a 100-year tenure. The company had earlier this year concluded a 50-year U.S. bond for a sum of $100 million. The bonds, with the longest-ever maturity by an Indian sovereign or corporate body, had been priced at a yield of 10.6 percent. Ministry sources said the company was not likely to get clearance for the entire sum. In their view an international borrowing of such duration required that the sum be pegged at $100 million.
FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS ALLOWED TO SET UP DEBT
FUNDS

The bourse regulator (SEBI) has decided to allow the foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to set up 100 percent debt funds. The finance minister has okayed the proposal. Separate registration procedures and an overall outer limit, to be set by the SEBI, form part the new guidelines. The money brought in by the 100 percent debt funds can be invested in debt instruments issued by corporates. The guidelines will help the FIIs bring in 100 percent of their dedicated funds through an alternative route. The existing system under which the FIIs are allowed to bring in money in the ratio of 30 percent debt and 70 percent equity will continue.
Business Line
BAYER ALLOWED 31 PCT STAKE IN ABS

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board cleared Bayer Industries (BIL) proposal to acquire a 31 percent stake in ABS Industries Ltd. BIL is a wholly owned subsidiary of the German multinational Bayer AG. However, the proposal is awaiting clearance from the main term lender, ICICI. Earlier, financial institutions were against the proposed preferential offer of 55,80,000 preference shares to BIL at a premium of 60 rupees per share, since it was not in consonance with institutional guidelines. The Unit Trust of India, the Life Insurance Corporation and ICICI jointly hold 17 percent of ABS's equity.
POWER MINISTRY FOR PUSH TO STATE-FUNDED PROJECTS

The power ministry is reverting to dependence on indigenous efforts and funds for quick completion of sanctioned and ongoing public sector power projects. This follows the low levels of enthusiasm among private and foreign investors. The fresh capacity addition strategy, following the dismal performance during the Eighth Plan owing to over-dependence on private and foreign investment, is being worked out in association with the Planning Commission. The Commission has assured adequate resource allocation for the implementation and completion of such projects which, till now, have been languishing for the lack of funds.
